name: Stockade
summary: Multi-tenant commerce teaching app with storefront, merchant operations, inventory and financial workflows.
reason: Master mentorship prompt and roadmap are proposals, not evidence that the learner has completed the curriculum.

name: Orchard Core
selectionReason: Tenant-aware dependency injection and persistence traces lead into post-commit side effects, idempotency and failure-design drills.

name: Twenty
selectionReason: Metadata-driven CRM architecture, permission-aware ORM flows and senior projects on outboxes, webhook delivery and contract tests.

name: Outline
selectionReason: Document mutation traces connect transactions, events, queues and WebSockets; multiple learning packs add ADRs, interview practice and a study plan.

name: NocoBase
selectionReason: Plugin lifecycle, resource actions, ACL and repository traces are paired with concrete pagination and mass-assignment exercises.

name: Infisical
selectionReason: Secret-write walkthroughs connect validation, authorization, data access and queues; drills address races, cache behavior and security boundaries.

name: Cal.diy
selectionReason: Booking, reservations, cancellation and webhook traces expose race conditions; scoped tickets turn those flows into hands-on work.

name: Teable
selectionReason: Record updates, recalculation and realtime synchronization connect to an incremental CQRS migration and source-based contribution exercises.

name: Formbricks
selectionReason: Survey response validation and browser SDK queues support junior tickets, architecture study and exercises across client/server boundaries.

name: Payload
selectionReason: Config-driven CMS behavior is traced through REST, hooks, authorization and database adapters, followed by contribution and design exercises.

name: Dify
selectionReason: Chat streaming, tenant boundaries, RAG and background work are explained through concrete flows and scoped implementation tickets.

name: Paperless-ngx
selectionReason: Upload-to-worker/OCR walkthroughs teach Django, Angular and background processing; contribution tasks connect failures to regression tests.

name: pretalx
selectionReason: Proposal workflows, persistent mail and versioned schedules provide concrete Django architecture lessons, failure analysis and junior tickets.

name: Mayan EDMS
selectionReason: Document ingestion, ACLs, event decorators and layered Celery workers provide broad operational and authorization learning with twenty starter tickets.

name: Zulip
selectionReason: Message delivery crosses Django actions and realtime event delivery; reading and contribution exercises make a large mixed-language system navigable.

name: Plane
selectionReason: Work-item flows connect Django, Celery, multiple React apps and realtime collaboration; guided tickets cover cross-service ownership.

name: Supabase Studio workspace
selectionReason: Extensive source-anchored lessons and missions distinguish server data, workspace state, table state, React Query and testable frontend boundaries.

name: Typebot
selectionReason: Tiered missions explain durable editor state versus transient graph state, with source excerpts, checkpoints and implementation/testing tracks.

name: OpenStatus
selectionReason: Monitoring architecture and inferred ADRs combine with practical missions about state ownership, cache invalidation and operational tradeoffs.

name: Novu
selectionReason: Notification infrastructure and codebase-health analysis are complemented by junior-to-senior missions on dashboard state, contracts and failure surfaces.

name: Hoppscotch
selectionReason: Request execution, GraphQL services, sandboxing and versioned schemas support detailed walkthroughs and invariant-focused contribution tickets.

name: Flagsmith
selectionReason: Flag evaluation, priority rules, caching and streaming become code-reading exercises and tenant-boundary test tickets.

name: Dub
selectionReason: Short-link redirects, attribution and transactional data expose hot-path/cache tradeoffs; the curriculum includes concrete junior contribution work.

name: Linkwarden
selectionReason: Bookmark writes, collection permissions, preservation workers and search indexing form an approachable full-stack architecture curriculum.

name: Postiz
selectionReason: Scheduling traces connect API, workers and durable workflows; exercises explicitly discuss the repository’s testing gaps rather than assuming coverage.

name: Umami
selectionReason: Analytics ingestion and query flows teach privacy, throughput, multiple storage backends and targeted testing through concrete tickets.

name: Open edX
selectionReason: Large LMS/authoring boundaries are paired with source-reading paths and predict-then-verify runtime drills with observable self-grading criteria.

name: ToolJet
selectionReason: Progressive missions connect React state, reusable hooks, API contracts and source-level design reasoning in a substantial application builder.

name: shadcn/ui
selectionReason: Registry, website and CLI boundaries teach code distribution and AST-based installation, with source excerpts and senior architecture missions.

name: NextCRM
selectionReason: Seven concrete CRM flows expose server actions, read/write authorization asymmetry, cache revalidation and testable cross-layer changes.

name: IDURAR
selectionReason: Authentication, generic CRUD and invoice flows explain dynamic controller discovery, reusable UI and domain-specific overrides through guided missions.

name: nopCommerce
selectionReason: Storefront, administration and plugin architecture support localized contribution tickets and a grounded ecommerce system-design exercise.

name: eShop / .NET Aspire
selectionReason: Distributed commerce flows, inferred ADRs and a 72-story bootcamp provide prerequisites, hints, acceptance criteria and operational capstones.

name: eShopOnWeb
selectionReason: A manageable monolith supports design-before-code feature tickets, authorization regression work and observable junior-to-senior learning rubrics.

name: CleanArchitecture
selectionReason: Multiple learning packs explain dependency direction, feature slices and tradeoffs, then add scoped contributions, ADRs and interview practice.

name: Bulletproof React
selectionReason: Source-based chapters and missions compare domain architecture across Vite and Next.js variants, with exercises on state and boundary ownership.

name: OpsForge
selectionReason: Nine detailed chapters connect production-oriented Next.js, data access, background work, testing and review of assisted code to concrete source.

name: JavaScript bootcamp and app labs
selectionReason: Extensive drills and coaching include multi-file debugging hunts, prediction checkpoints and spaced practice tied to executable application files.

name: Morphic
selectionReason: Streaming AI answers, tool execution, persistence and caching form explicit request traces with test-oriented contribution exercises.

name: Warband
selectionReason: Architecture and postmortems teach server authority, deterministic retries, time and database uniqueness; exercises reproduce specific failure classes.

name: Atlas
selectionReason: A full sprint curriculum connects domain modeling to durable outboxes and webhook delivery, with ADRs, flaw analysis and review exercises.

name: Folio
selectionReason: Progressive collaboration lessons develop identity, ordering, tombstones and CRDT convergence through source-based experiments and fuzzing.

name: Tracer
selectionReason: The issue-tracker curriculum progresses from REST to offline synchronization, mutation logs and realtime delivery with explicit failure/review lessons.

name: Relay
selectionReason: Workflow-engine sprints teach durable execution, retries, connectors and DAG validation using concrete graph cases and implementation tradeoffs.

name: Harbor
selectionReason: Support and retrieval lessons teach evaluation before feature expansion, chunking/search tradeoffs and traceable sprint-level engineering decisions.

name: Pulse analytics
selectionReason: A progressive analytics course links ingestion and insights to storage migration, workload measurement and documented operational exercises.

name: Agora
selectionReason: Commerce sprints and ADRs connect cart/domain events and promotion extensibility to design alternatives and code-review reasoning.

name: Bazaar
selectionReason: Fifteen commerce sprints explain cart behavior, caching and consistency across buyer and merchant surfaces, with explicit teaching-adapter limits.

name: Perch
selectionReason: A progressive PR-oriented course provides learner guidance, local sprint narratives and final restore/incident ownership exercises.

name: Indico
selectionReason: A large event platform is made approachable through request-handler/data-layer maps and concrete task, authorization and cleanup-test tickets.

name: Saleor
selectionReason: GraphQL commerce cartography and contribution tasks introduce transaction tracing, checkout contracts and source-grounded engineering reasoning.
